output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (IS/IS NOT by reason, tenure, timing), then evidence-ledger check of the manager's account, then competing-hypotheses weighing
output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is almost certainly caused by the 14 April Finance change. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the same week. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, and non-referred calls still resolve at 82%, both unchanged. Billing resolution fell from 79% to 56%, while other call types barely moved. The April intake is not the cause. Tenured agents fell from 75% to about 67%, the same as the new starters, who refer at about the same rate. The tariff rise added tariff calls, but those resolve at 85%, so it isn't the cause. The IVR change came later, on 28 April, and FCR had already dropped. Workload isn't supported either. I'm fairly sure of this (about 85–90%). Next steps: don't put the April intake on performance plans, since that would penalise the wrong group. Agree a higher credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling of credits. That is what Finance's controller said they would consider. Track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate before any wider rollout. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence.
